That's not really the  performance we've come to expect. 
No, I think, um, I just spoke to the boys  there about it. Rangers can beat you. I mean,  
Rangers have so many obvious advantages.  You can lose a game 2-0 or 3-0 here if they  
turn up and show their quality. I thought in  the first half, in general, we competed well  
enough. You’d say Rangers were the better team  throughout—of course, they were—but there was a  
bit of determination about us, a shape about  us that allowed us to stay in the game.
We lose a goal when you're praying VAR  gets you a hand, but at the end of the day,  
I had a feeling that wasn’t going to happen.  Ultimately, it comes from a throw-in,  
and we don't do enough to stop the cross. We  just allow Hagi to put the ball in the box,  
and Tav is more determined  to get on the end of it.
At half-time, we spoke about needing to see more.  I think Rangers’ movement—Eigemann coming toward  
the ball and Hagi coming in off the shape—caused  everybody a problem. In general, they've got  
good players at the top end of the pitch, and the  movement they’ve got caused us issues. It didn’t  
really help that we were already a couple of  defenders down, and it was a patched-up back four.
We decided at half-time to take  that decision-making out and try  
to go 4-4-2 against them, to get two  center-halves tight. But it became  
pretty obvious we couldn’t cope with that.  Once the second and third goals went in,  
it was all about trying to stop the bleeding.  Unfortunately for us, it does matter—it should  
matter to players—that losing a game 2-0  or 3-0 is different from losing 5-0 or 6-0.
But we felt sorry for ourselves. We failed  to get the fundamentals right: stop your man,  
stop the cross, get tight in the box. Yes, Rangers  were clinical, they had their tails up, and they  
started to enjoy the game. I think once we flooded  the midfield, we stopped their front lot from  
enjoying the game a bit. But then they started  going outside us, and we didn’t stop crosses.
It was a horrible night for us. It shows what can  happen if you don’t keep your determination, your  
concentration, and your head. A horrible night for  us—not acceptable to lose in that type of manner.
We now need to get back to being the team we were.  Six weeks ago, we beat Rangers. A few weeks ago,  
we beat Hearts. Forty-five minutes of a strong  performance on Saturday. We've never been hit like  
that this season, and it has to be a reference  for us going forward. We need to go to Dundee  
United on Saturday, and the first priority is to  try to keep a clean sheet and get some confidence  
back into our defensive work. That’s what we’ll  try to do, and we’ll move on from this quickly.
Joe Wright? He went to the hospital  
for a scan, so we’ll wait and see. We  weren’t even allowed to use that as a  
concussion sub. We wanted to get Marley  Watkins off at the end but apparently  
didn’t notify the referee quickly enough.  We’ll need to wait and see how Joe is.
His head or jaw? Head.
You spoke a little bit about the defense there.  There’s only been one clean sheet in the league  
this season. With that result tonight, Kilmarnock  have conceded the most goals in the league. This  
is largely the same defense as last season  when you were so solid. What’s behind that? 
I don’t want to put too much on it, but I  do think Stokes Finley is a massive loss  
for us—I’ll be honest with that. But we can’t harp  on about it; we have to deal with what we’ve got.
We’ve always tried to be quite positive. We get  the benefit of going with two wide players and two  
strikers, and in the main, we’ve tried to do  that. But there’s a trade-off when you come  
up against teams that play a bit more direct  or better teams. You have to be able to cope  
and defend man-for-man a lot of the time.  Unfortunately, we’ve not done it with the  
same confidence or aggressive manner to try to  stop the opponent from getting opportunities.
I think we’ve just been a bit too easy to play  against. Like I said, I thought we were all right  
in the game, but the first goal is important,  especially here. Rangers were coming off the back  
of scrutiny, and you don’t want to give them a leg  up. We spoke about that, but we allowed a cross  
into the box, and Tavernier—a full-back—is  more determined to get on the end of it.
All these little things matter. We go as we are.  We’ve got some better games ahead. Obviously,  
the imbalance of playing away games to home games  has been quite pivotal. We need to start being  
a team that can cope away from home and get  back to being a winning team at home again.
